summary: My own DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE/DEPTH scaling experiments crashed (192/256 don't divide TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, 256 OOMs at 128 depth-8) or queued too long to complete before GPU contention cleared. I then applied a 4-change recipe recalled from prior-session memory (not from this cell's peers): TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19->2^18, ASPECT_RATIO 64->96 (width not depth, model_dim 768), sliding window short=long//8 instead of //2, and has_ve on first3+last3 layers instead of alternating placement. This took val_bpb from baseline 0.997359 to 0.977903. As my own variations on top, I tested WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.3 (worse: 0.981864) and DEPTH 8->10 at matched model_dim=768 (worse: 0.991183, OOM at full batch so had to halve DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE/double grad_accum which likely also hurt), both disconfirmed. Next things worth trying: shorter sliding windows still (//16), tuning ADAM_BETAS or SCALAR_LR which are untested levers, or reducing WEIGHT_DECAY given the smaller effective batch now takes more optimizer steps per budget.
